newsitem.title: UK: UK stock strategists stand by year-end forecasts.
newsitem.headline: UK stock strategists stand by year-end forecasts.

text.p: Stock market strategists were on Thursday mostly standing by their year-end forecasts for Britain's FTSE 100 index despite a buoyant start to the year which has helped prompt a flurry of upgrades to expectations.

Just seven weeks into 1997 the FTSE 100 has already surpassed the year-end targets set by many stock market pundits, yet most are standing by their forecasts ahead of what could be a tricky year for shares round the world.
Earlier this week Nick Knight, strategist at Japanese investment bank Nomura, bumped up his year-end forecast to 4,800 from 4,400, making him among the most optimistic pundits on the London market.

Separately Mark Brown at brokerage ABN AMRO Hoare Govett nudged up his cautious prediction to 4,000 from 3,900, largely reflecting a view that the pound will stay strong against the German mark, damping the British economy and warding off inflation.
Most brokerages however said they were sticking to their forecasts for the end of 1997, preferring to wait at least until after the election, which must be held before the end of May.

"The one big thing that might cause us to re-evaluate the year-end picture is if there was a decisive fiscal tightening at the other side of the election," said Paul O'Connor, UK stock market strategist at BZW, the broking arm of Barclays Bank .
"That would take the pressure off sterling, bonds and short-term interest rates and would be a very positive background for the market".
After hitting a record 4,362.4 early on Thursday, some six percent above its level at the end of 1996, the index ended the day 1.6 points lower at 4,355.8.
An ever-present risk is that Wall Street will suffer a long-expected fall after its rip-roaring run carried it to record highs above the 7,000 level earlier this month.

"We're forecasting 4,350 (for the FTSE) based on our forecast for a strong correction in the Dow down to 5,800," said Andrew Smith, pan-European equity strategist at brokerage Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.

"With that in mind there's obviously going to be a severe correction across Europe and within the FTSE," Smith said. "But if the Dow doesn't come off as strongly as we expect, we think the FTSE will end the year at about 4,600."
Analysts were also holding fire until after the next round of company results before reviewing their predictions.

"There's a lot that can happen between now and the end of the year," said Savvas Savouri, strategist at brokerage Credit Lyonnais Laing. "We still have the reporting season and that will test whether these levels are sustainable".
Savouri predicted the FTSE would finish this year at 4,450.
Meantime with sterling still looking bullish, the strong currency could dampen company profits.

"Earnings are going to stay under pressure throughout the year unless there's a decisive weakening of sterling, which we're not looking for," said BZW's O'Connor, who forecasts the FTSE at 4,300 by year-end.
Shares may wait until the second half of the year before they wobble, some analysts said.
Richard Jeffrey, economist at brokerage Charterhouse Tilney, predicted the market would top out at around 4,400 by mid-year, before dipping to 4,000 by the year end.

Jeffrey said he expected strong consumer growth to fan inflationary pressure, in turn leading to monetary policy tightening. "I think the market will have a touch of the nerves in the second half," he said.
